summary: Hertha Krick was an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Vienna (~1965–1972) under doctoral supervisor Gerhard Oberhammer (~1968–1972). She subsequently served as an assistant at the University of Vienna from 1972 to 1979.

Hervey DeWitt Griswold worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Union College, Union Theological Seminary, Oxford, Berlin, and Cornell (PhD ~1900). He served as Professor of Philosophy at Forman Christian College (1894–1914) and Visiting Lecturer at Columbia (1923–1929).

Hew McLeod was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history. Educated at Nelson College, the University of Otago (~1950–1954), and SOAS University of London (~1962–1965), he later held an editorial board post (Redaktionsråd) at Otago (attested 2005).

Heymann Steinthal worked in linguistics and philosophy, studying under August Boeckh at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1843–1847). He later held posts at Berlin (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, under Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He served as professor at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 1996–2003).
Hidehiko Kurita is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who earned a PhD from Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2020).

Hidehiro Okada specialized in history, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Washington under Nicholas Poppe. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1968–1993) and Tokiwa University (~1996–2002).
Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).
Hidemasa Nagata specialized in history and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1952 to 1960 and later held a post there from ~1966 to 1997.

Hidenaka Tanaka was a scholar of linguistics who studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo, Oxford, and Kyoto University (Doctor of Letters, 1930). He held posts at Tokyo, Kyoto University (1920; 1931–1946), and Kyoto Women's University (~1950–1974).

Hidenori Kitagawa specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, having studied under Hakuju Ui. He was a fellow at the Rockefeller Foundation (1952–1953) and served as a professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969).

Hidenori S. Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as professor at Shitennoji University and University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Taisho University and Waseda University. He was a longtime professor at Waseda (1968–1998) and Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1966–2003).

Hideomi Yaita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1977–1983). He worked as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1983–1997) and taught at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hidetaka Fukazawa is a scholar of religious studies who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1976–1980) and held a post at Hitotsubashi University from ~1993 to 2020.
Hidetaka Nakatani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under the supervision of Gadjin Nagao.
Hideto Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University (~1963–1972) and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies affiliated with Taisho University, serving there as a researcher (1998), lecturer (2008), and chief research fellow (2017), as well as a research student at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (2006).

Hidetsugu Yagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909) and later held academic posts at Tohoku University (~1919–1932), Osaka University (~1932–1946), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and the University of Tokyo (~1946–1947).
